newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity ends up on gas rally, cold temps.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity ends up on gas rally, cold temps.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures finished the week sharply higher on a rally in natural gas prices and expected pickup in heating demand tied to colder temperatures in the Pacific Northwest next week.
The electricity complex today broke out of this week's rangebound trading as NYMEX January Henry Hub natgas futures posted new life-of-contract highs.

Despite lingering concerns over recent heavy rainfall and early building of snowpack in the Northwest, and their impact on hydroelectric production in the spring, movement in the natural gas market remained the primary driver of western electricity prices, market sources said.
The January Henry Hub contract settled up 32.2 cents at $3.851 per million British thermal units after trading as high as $3.870.
In the West, January gas deliveries to the San Juan/Blanco Hub ended near $3.35, off from the day's high in the $3.40 area, but still markedly higher than Thursday's $3.19-$3.22.
January California-Oregon Border (COB) futures settled at $25.50 a megawatt hour (MWh), up $1.05 after reaching as high as $25.75.
February COB finished up 55 cents at $19.50, its session high. Other active COB contracts ended 35 to 55 cents higher.
January Palo Verde (PV) futures settled at $25.60, up 92 cents after hitting a high of $26.00.
February PV finished up 87 cents at $20.30 after traded between $20.10 and $20.75. Deferred PV months ended flat ot 70 cents higher.
Some participants noted there were some signs of easing in late trading after the day's sharp run-up.
"Things are awfully high...COB is coming down a little," said a New York broker.
Most brokers and traders expect the electricity contracts to continue taking cues from gas prices, which are expected to climb again Monday.
"I think if anyone's interested, people should be looking to buy," a Houston trader said.

Two coal-fired power units, which were unexpectedly shut earlier this week, would resume operation by this weekend: a 865 megawatt (MW) unit 2 at the Intermountain power plant in Delta, Utah and a 550 MW unit at the Jim Bridger plant near Rock Springs, Wyo.
NYMEX estimated 385 COB and 200 PV contracts were sold.
